en.name: Cornelius
en.summary: A pope who faced a rival claimant to his office over the deeply divisive question of whether Christians who had lapsed under persecution could be readmitted to the church.
en.body: Cornelius's election came in the aftermath of the Decian persecution, which had forced the question of how to treat the large number of Christians who had complied with the order to sacrifice to Roman gods rather than face death. Cornelius favored a path of penance and eventual reconciliation for the lapsed, a position that provoked the priest Novatian to have himself set up as a rival, rigorist pope who held that such sinners could never be readmitted. The dispute produced one of the early church's most consequential schisms, with Novatian's followers persisting as a separate movement for centuries. Cornelius was exiled during a renewed persecution and died, likely from the hardship of exile, and is venerated as a martyr.
